note: No fully worked numerical calculation examples (with input loads, step-by-step arithmetic, and a final designed reinforcement quantity) are present in this chunk. The source provides generic Model Details (essentially reusable templates) and one illustrative untensioned-reinforcement LAYOUT example for a prestressed flat slab, plus a tendon-profile numerical table. These are captured below as the closest available 'examples'.

example_1_untensioned_reinforcement_layo.fact_type: DIRECTLY STATED (figure content), partially INFERRED (overall layout logic)

source.caption: Example of untensioned reinforcement layout for an unbonded system

example_1_untensioned_reinforcement_layo.context: Floor plan showing reinforcement bars (not tendons) required in the top of the slab at columns and prestressing anchorages, and in the bottom of slab at mid-span, for an unbonded post-tensioned flat slab.
example_1_untensioned_reinforcement_layo.engineering_takeaway: Reinforcement is concentrated and grouped near columns (typical column bar groups repeated at each of several column positions, e.g. 12 no. per column type), with U-bar groups used at slab edges/mid-span, and a fabric sheet (A193) supplementing distributed reinforcement — consistent with the general rule (§7.4.1) that flat slabs need top un-tensioned reinforcement at columns and sometimes bottom reinforcement at mid-span.
example_1_untensioned_reinforcement_layo.drawing_implication: The reinforcement drawing is prepared SEPARATELY from the post-tensioning profile drawing (explicit rule, not just this example) — i.e. two overlapping but distinct drawing layers/sheets for the same slab.

example_2_tendon_profile_numerical_table.engineering_takeaway: Demonstrates the actual tabular format used to set out a curved tendon profile: two coordinates (y = height above soffit, z = distance from outside/end face) are given at 5%-of-span intervals near the anchorage, for each of (here) two tendons in a row. This is directly reusable as a data structure for a parametric duct-profile generator (see 10_generator.py).

example_3_band_beam_and_slab_layout.fact_type: DIRECTLY STATED (dimensions transcribed from OCR of a dimensioned drawing)

source.caption: Typical tendon profile in a post-tensioned band beam and slab

example_3_band_beam_and_slab_layout.context: Full-floor plan showing column grid (gridlines 21-39 vertically, 1-20 horizontally), tendon spacing dimensions (numerous vertical dimension strings such as '150 65 35 70', '2500', '1250', repeating per bay), slab/beam thickness note.

key_dimensions_stated.bay_dimensioning_pattern: Repeating dimension groups of the general form 40/80/120/440(or 425/390)/120/80/40 across each beam width, with tendon 'high point' sections dimensioned separately (Fig 7.32b) showing cover callouts of 25, 30, 40, 50mm at different chair heights (425/405 Chair).

example_3_band_beam_and_slab_layout.engineering_takeaway: Illustrates that a band-beam-and-slab post-tensioned floor is dimensioned as a repeating parametric bay pattern (grid spacing × standard beam cross-section profile), which supports a generator design where one bay's tendon/cover profile is defined once and repeated across the grid — see 10_generator.py `create_band_beam_bay()`.
example_3_band_beam_and_slab_layout.caveat: OCR of this dense engineering drawing is unreliable for exact numeric reconstruction; treat the specific numbers as illustrative/approximate, not verified. Flagged in 12_unresolved_questions.md.
